title: Ticket ID 1783734920012010
text:
Ticket ID: 1783734920012010  Ken Novich
I ordered 8 Alfordson Dining Chairs from Temu with confirmation stating Free Delivery. After a couple of weeks, Temu cancelled the order stating “The supplier could not supply”. I figured they were out of stock. I went back online to find a replacement and found the exact same chairs were still being available, so I re-ordered them and received confirmation including Free Delivery. I had paid for both orders and received a credit for the first cancelled order. A couple of weeks passed during which time I had given my old chairs to a charity company. After a couple of weeks, I received the same cancellation for the 2nd order and another refund.
I contacted Alfordson to find out what they had that was similar but was told that they had no record of my name on orders from Temu and that stock was available and still was. As I had disposed of my old chairs, I easily found several other retailers offering the same chairs but instead of Free Delivery, I had to pay $139. I placed an order with BigW and received delivery in 2 days. Temu keep sending me details about how to contact Alfordson, totally ignoring that I have told them that I already have and Temu have not been truthful with me.
I went onto the Temu chat line and complained that since Temu had accepted my order twice with Free Delivery, that they should reimburse me for the delivery charge I had to pay BigW. These so called “Customer Service” staff were next to useless. I spent an hour being passed from one to the other and eventually requested a Supervisor after being told that Alfordson could not deliver as there was an “Anomoly”. Nobody will explain what that means. Since then I have explained the entire fiasco to 5 different supervisors (Augustus, Austin, Alethea, Lily, Emman.)  None of them are prepared to answer my questions…. Do they admit that the orders were never placed? ….Before cancelling them, why could they not contact me? …..Why do they totally ignore what I have written to them and sending a standard computer reply?
They must run a special course on how to be vague and evasive. p.s. They did provide $10 credit for all the inconvenience and a promised 20% discount on my next order. I daresay this offer will probably be cancelled after this review. There are many dates involved so I have just mentioned the last.

title: Temu are inferior quality and when…
text:
Temu are inferior quality and when leaving a review about a product, I was told my review was removed due to it being spam. It was a short, honest review. I wonder how many people also have negative reviews removed for this reason. Temu refund speedily for bad quality products. Clothing is hit and miss, the fabrics can often smell chemically and this doesnt always wash out. All in all, most products I have ordered have not as expected and very disappointing. The angel candle holders were plastic, which could be very dangerous if people used a lit candle as opposed to a battery operated tea light.     The tarot and oracle cards are copies of well known Hay House decks such as Doreen Virtue and Rebecca Campbell and AI decks. They dont come in a box with a booklet like the quality hay house products, but in a cardboard sleeve with a qr code to find the meanings. 
I ordered 'genuine' crystals that were plastic coated beads made to look real, and crystal semi precious beads that were glass! The Bra wires are unsafe and go rusty and brittle very quickly, they are not reliable sizing, in comparison to high street bras in the UK. 
Delivery is speedy, around 5-7 days, packed in plastic bags which isnt always enough packaging for the more fragile items, so they can arrive broken or chipped (as in the case of wood effect garden signs).

title: Temu = FRAUD
text:
Temu = FRAUD! 
Beyond selling cheap, low-quality products, Temu’s aggressive and misleading marketing tactics feel like dealing with a professional con artist. Recently, Temu sent me a promotion claiming I could select up to eight free gifts. Curious to see whether the offer was legitimate, I decided to test it. 
I carefully selected eight items that were advertised as free and added one additional item priced at approximately $17. After completing the purchase and placing the order, I waited to see if the promotion would be honored. 
The result? I received only the one item that I actually paid for. 
None of the eight supposedly "free" items ever arrived. Whether through fine print, hidden conditions, or intentionally confusing marketing, the end result was the same: the advertised free gifts never materialized. To me, this experience was the very definition of deceptive advertising—promising customers something valuable to entice a purchase, then failing to deliver on that promise. 
If a company advertises free products to convince customers to place an order, those products should actually show up. Based on my experience, Temu's promotion created the expectation that I would receive eight free gifts, yet only the paid item was delivered. I came away feeling misled, disappointed, and far less trusting of any future promotions they advertise. 
Call to Action: Consumers Deserve Better

Consumers should not have to navigate confusing promotions, hidden conditions, or marketing campaigns that create unrealistic expectations. If you've had a similar experience, don't simply write it off as the cost of doing business. Document what was advertised, save screenshots, keep your order confirmations, and speak up. 
Consider sharing your experience through consumer review platforms and, where appropriate, reporting potentially misleading advertising practices to consumer protection agencies. Companies should be held accountable when their marketing creates expectations that are not fulfilled. The more consumers report questionable practices, the easier it becomes for regulators to identify patterns and protect the public from deceptive marketing tactics. 
Transparency, honesty, and accountability should be the standard—not the exception. If enough consumers demand fair treatment and accurate advertising, companies will be forced to compete based on trust and value rather than confusion and gimmicks. 
Buyer beware: If an offer sounds too good to be true, take screenshots, read the fine print carefully, and keep records of everything. My experience serves as a reminder that "free" offers are not always what they appear to be, and consumers must remain vigilant to protect themselves from potentially deceptive marketing practices.

title: Temu Repeatedly cancelling legitimate paid orders under the vague excuse of "unusual activity"
text:
I used Temu several times last year and placed around five orders without a single issue. This year has been a completely different experience.

In January, I placed an order and paid through PayPal. A few hours later, Temu cancelled it, claiming there was an issue with my payment method. I accepted it as a one-time mistake.

Three days ago, I decided to give Temu another chance. This time I paid with my bank card through PayPal. The order remained in processing for three days, so I naturally expected it to ship. Instead, Temu cancelled it again and gave me the exact same excuse:

> "Refund automatically issued by Temu due to unusual activity. It needs to be processed by your financial institution."

This explanation makes no sense. I use the same bank card and the same PayPal account on Amazon, AliExpress, eBay, and many other online marketplaces. I have placed hundreds of orders over the years without a single payment issue. The problem is clearly not my payment method.

The worst part is that Temu waits days before cancelling the order, wasting customers' time while they expect their package to be shipped. If there is truly a payment problem, why not reject the order immediately instead of leaving it in processing for days?

This has been an incredibly frustrating experience. From my perspective, ordering from Temu has become a waste of time. Repeatedly cancelling legitimate paid orders under the vague excuse of "unusual activity" without providing any meaningful explanation is unacceptable. Unless Temu fixes this issue and improves its verification process, I won't be ordering from them again, and I cannot recommend the platform based on my recent experience.

title: BEWARE INFLATED CUSTOMS IMPORT DUTY
text:
Reading the small print it appears to say that €3 is added to every item for customs duty.

Therefore a small low value item can escalate by 300-400% in price.

Given they know what they will add it is very evasive to still show the pre duty cost not the final cost and only add a lump figure at checkout which with my multi items was around double expectation.

I have no idea of each items full cost and probably would have deleted all low value items after the reality check.

Fortunately my gym shirts, shorts and gloves were a good saving so it’s not the overall value that worries me.  The misrepresentation does.

I have paid customs on many cross border items and there is no way the total import duty for one small bag valued at about €109 should be €44 without an actual customs validation receipt.

BEWARE INFLATED CUSTOMS CHARGES

EDIT:

You have requested specific details of my purchase in relation to a generic statement.

All you need to justify is the €3 charge on for instance 5 items I bought between €0.66 and €0.96 which appear to have gone from about €4 total to €19.

“Import charges:     43,56€

For orders shipped from outside the EU with a value of €150 or less, Temu will charge import charges of €3 per different item in the order, plus applicable VAT. For this purpose, the same items will be counted only once.”

How does the import duty on a €0.66 item get charged at €3 and where is the proof that Spanish Customs made that charge.

Vague non specific information which in my opinion from paying no more than €7 on any other item I have received across Spains EU border makes it seem like profit inflation not a genuine fee. 

Please provide proof customs charge a minimum per item fee of €3 or the truth will be obvious.

EDIT AND RESPONSE

It is clear that you do not want to answer my question for everyone to read.  That tells everyone all they need to know about the mythical Customs duty of in my case up to 5x the item value.

Sellers of small value items will see sales evaporate once customers notice this obvious back door inflation so well done damaging their small income as I am sure they won’t be getting the money.

Given Customs fees are paid by the recipient receiving the parcel once Spanish Customs assess the individual parcel it is also illogical to put a guessed fee on each item.

I will not be speculating with any small cost items as whilst I was happy to bin the “junk” I am not willing to pay a premium now to do so.

What once felt like a fun and affordable shopping experience now feels like a game designed to confuse customers.

Shopping on Temu should not require customers to act like private investigators just to understand pricing, credits, and checkout charges.

There was a time when I genuinely enjoyed recommending Temu to friends and family. Today, I find myself questioning almost every offer, promotion, and transaction before placing an order.

Temu needs to do better. Customers deserve transparency, honesty, and a straightforward shopping experience—not confusion disguised as savings.

I checked my bank and noticed my account wasn’t refunded.  Contacted CS and to my surprise they said oh you have to initiate the refund process.  That on Halara not me. While I enjoy the clothes the process needs to overhauled.  I hope you do better.

title: Purchase Review
text:
Good afternoon,

I recently received the pearl earrings I ordered for my daughter. To ensure I had made a good purchase, I took them to a respected family-owned jeweler in Bethesda, Maryland, that has been in business for more than 70 years.

After examining the earrings, they shared that while the pearls were of acceptable quality, they were not exceptional. They also noted that the pearls appeared to be approximately 8mm, even though I specifically requested the larger size within the advertised range (8.5mm).

When I asked about value, they estimated that, without the branding, packaging, marketing, and online presence, the earrings would likely retail in the $350–$400 range. I even considered purchasing a pair from them and returning yours. However, the jeweler candidly advised that the time and effort involved in making the return likely would not be worth the difference. I appreciated their honesty, particularly since it meant they did not make a sale.

Needless to say, I was disappointed to hear this assessment and equally disappointed with the product I received. I find it difficult to believe that no one has raised similar concerns in the past, although I understand I have no way of knowing.

I wanted to share this feedback in the hope that you will review the quality and sizing of the pearls being sold, as the product I received did not meet the expectations created by your descriptions.

title: Once, shame on you. Twice, shame on me.
text:

Dear Customer,

Regarding your order #3074703395752487, we sincerely apologize for the unpleasant experience you’ve had and for not receiving your package as expected.

According to the logistics tracking information, the status of your parcel is marked as "Delivered." However, we fully understand and take seriously your feedback that you did not actually receive the package. We recognize how concerning and frustrating this situation can be, and we truly appreciate your patience.

Please note that once a package arrives in the destination country, the final delivery is handled by the local postal service or courier provider. In accordance with our dispute resolution policy, we kindly recommend contacting your local post office or delivery company directly to further verify the actual delivery details—for example, whether it was delivered to a neighbor, placed in a mailbox, or left at a pickup point due to missed delivery attempts.

If it is confirmed that the package was indeed not delivered or has been lost, we kindly ask you to request an official **"Undelivered Proof"** or **"Lost Parcel Certificate"** from the relevant authority. The document should include the following:

- The tracking number of the parcel  
- A clear statement confirming the failure of delivery or loss of the package  
- An official stamp, agency logo, or electronic signature as valid authentication  
- If provided via email, please include a full screenshot showing the sender’s email address, subject line, and message body  

Once we receive a valid proof that meets these requirements, we will immediately submit it for review and proceed with the appropriate resolution, such as a refund or compensation, as quickly as possible.

For your convenience, below are the recommended contact details for the local logistics provider:  Chronopost.

Thank you sincerely for your understanding and cooperation throughout this process. Should you have any questions or updates, please don’t hesitate to reply to this email—we are always here to support you.

Wishing you all the best and smooth days ahead!

Best regards,  
AliExpress Customer Service Team

NO! I will not waste another second on your red tape.

title: Poor after-sales support when a defective product is delivered
text:
I purchased a hair brush through AliExpress and unfortunately received a defective product.

I understand that manufacturing defects can happen with any company. My disappointment is not with the defect itself, but with how AliExpress handles these situations.

The only solutions offered were:

accept a small partial refund and keep a defective product; or
package the item myself, travel to a post office, and complete the entire return process in order to receive a full refund.

The issue is not the product's value (around US$10). The issue is the principle.

As a good-faith customer, I fulfilled my part of the contract: I selected the product, paid for it, and waited for delivery. The defective product was entirely the seller's responsibility. Nevertheless, AliExpress transferred the burden of solving the problem to me, requiring me to spend my own time and effort on a return process that I never agreed to when I made the purchase.

When everything goes well, delivery is made to my home. When something goes wrong because of the supplier, I'm expected to become part of their reverse logistics operation.

I find this policy unfair and contrary to what good customer service should look like. I expected AliExpress to take responsibility for resolving a problem it caused, instead of transferring the inconvenience to the customer.

I hope the company reviews this policy and adopts a more customer-friendly approach in cases where defective products are delivered.

title: A month of broken promises over a return shipping refund
text:
I’ve been going in circles with AliExpress support for over a month now, and I’m writing this because at this point nothing else has worked.

The short version: I returned an item and paid for the return shipping myself, on the express understanding that it would be refunded. That wasn’t me assuming anything. Before the package even reached the seller, support told me in chat to keep the proof of payment because the shipping would be refunded once the return was complete. The return form in the app said the same. And the shipping cost was almost as much as the item itself, so if anyone had told me it was on me, I’d never have sent it back. It wouldn’t have been worth it.

Then it just became a wall.

July 7, they confirmed in writing: the shipping fee would be refunded based on the receipt. July 8, I sent the receipt, and there’s a logged reply on their side proving it. July 9, they closed the case saying they never got a valid response. That’s simply not true, and their own system shows it.

After that their escalation team offered a coupon as the refund format, and confirmed it twice, once on July 14. Issued within 1 to 5 business days if I replied within 24 hours. I replied on July 15, inside their own deadline. The coupon never showed up in my account. Not once. What I got instead was another email telling me no refund was possible at all.

So they promised, ignored my reply, closed the case for “silence,” then offered a coupon themselves, I accepted, and now it’s suddenly impossible. Every step of that is documented in their own emails.

What actually gets me isn’t even the money. It’s the lying. Different agents, same recycled lines, and a written promise from their own senior team that they’re now pretending never happened. A month of that.

If you’re reading this while deciding whether to buy from them: keep every screenshot, don’t trust a verbal or chat promise, and know that “we’ll refund it” can quietly turn into “policy says no” the moment the item’s back with the seller.

I still just want the coupon they already promised me in writing. That’s all.

title: What I wish I'd known before buying cycling clothing from AliExpress.
text:
I purchased three items of cycling clothing from AliExpress for almost NZ$200. For varying reasons the items were unsuitable and not what I expected.The fabric quality was generally good, but the after-sales experience and dispute process were extremely disappointing. 
Here's what I wish I'd known before ordering.
1. Don't assume the published size guide is accurate.
I ordered one jersey according to the seller's published body measurements. My chest and waist measurements fell within the advertised size range, yet the jersey was significantly too small to wear. I supplied evidence of my body measurements + the seller's size chart and measurements of the actual garment, but my claim was rejected (no valid reason given).
2. Product photos don't always tell the full story.
A second cycling jersey looked excellent online, but the rear pockets were positioned much higher than every other well-fitting cycling jersey that I own. Rear pockets are an essential functional feature for cyclists. Their high-up-the-back position made them difficult and impractical to access while riding. I supplied comparison photographs and measurements to demonstrate the difference. Their response was the standard:- Your request was closed as the supporting information you provided was not sufficient.
3. Check that the product you receive actually matches the listing.
A thermal cycling vest was advertised with three rear pockets, but the vest I received had no rear pockets at all. I provided photographs and screenshots of the listing to demonstrate the difference.
4. Expect to provide extensive evidence if something goes wrong.
I supplied photographs, measurements, screenshots, comparison images and detailed written explanations for every dispute. Be prepared to document everything from the moment your parcel arrives.
5. Don't expect the dispute process to explain its decisions.
My disputes and appeals were repeatedly rejected with generic statements that my evidence was "insufficient", but without explaining why or addressing the specific evidence I had submitted. My evidence clearly demonstrated the issue. This left me with the impression that my submissions had not been truly considered. 
6. Returning an item is not as straightforward as it sounds.
AliExpress eventually agreed that I could return the vest, but only after paying international return postage to China upfront (which is almost as much as the cost of item itself). Although the seller is stated to be responsible for return shipping where an item is not as described, there was no clear or reliable assurance that I would be reimbursed in cash. The guidance also refers to reimbursement by AliExpress coupon in some circumstances, which is of limited value if you no longer wish to shop on the platform.
7. The biggest risk isn't the clothing - it's the after-sales process.
My greatest disappointment wasn't that some items weren't suitable. It was the dispute process itself, which I found opaque, inconsistent and unnecessarily difficult despite making every effort to provide the requested evidence and resolve matters professionally with both the sellers and AliExpress. In my experience, the process eventually reached a point where there was no meaningful opportunity to discuss or clarify the issues further, even though I still had additional evidence and unanswered questions. I was left feeling that the process had become procedural rather than focused on achieving a fair outcome.
8. This experience changed my buying behaviour.
I have purchased many items through other online marketplaces and have always found the returns process straightforward, transparent and customer-focused. This experience with AliExpress has had the opposite effect. Rather than building confidence in the platform, it has reinforced my preference to shop elsewhere. Price is important, but trust, fairness and responsive customer service are ultimately what determine where I choose to spend my money.
My conclusion
Based on this experience, I will not purchase through AliExpress again. If you do choose to buy, do so knowing that you may waste your money and have nothing to show for it. Even though I demonstrated strong evidence, all my time and efforts got me nowhere. So by all means, take screenshots of every product listing, keep all correspondence and photograph every item as soon as it arrives – but know this may get you nowhere. I hope your experience is better than mine, but I believe buyers should understand the risks & potential difficulties of the returns and dispute process before ordering.
